title: Light and Colour
summary: How light travels in straight lines, how a prism splits white light and why the sky is blue.

steps.title: Light travels in straight lines
sentences: Light moves in straight lines, which is why shadows have clear shapes.
It is the fastest thing in the universe, about three hundred thousand kilometres every second.
Light from the Sun takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.

steps.title: A rainbow in a prism
sentences: White light is a mix of all the colours.
When it passes through a glass prism or raindrops, each colour bends by a different amount and spreads out.
The colours always appear in the same order: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red.

steps.title: Why things have colour
sentences: A red apple looks red because it reflects red light and soaks up the other colours.
A white paper reflects almost all colours, and a black cloth absorbs most of them.
That is why a black shirt feels hotter in the Sun.

steps.title: Blue sky, red sunset
sentences: Air spreads the blue part of sunlight in all directions more than the red part, so the sky looks blue.
At sunset the light travels through more air, the blue is scattered away, and the red and orange remain.
A rainbow needs sunshine behind you and rain in front of you.

facts: There is no sound in space, but light travels through the emptiness of space.
The moon shines only by reflected sunlight.
Some animals, such as bees, can see ultraviolet light that humans cannot see.

quiz.q: Which colour is at one end of the rainbow?
quiz.why: Red is at the outer edge and violet at the inner edge.

quiz.q: Why does a red apple look red?
quiz.why: It reflects red light and absorbs most other colours.

quiz.q: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
